mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 declines by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contractions exceeding 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500K units for four consecutive months signals a weakening residential construction sector, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of HOUST below 500K.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically coincides with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average.
